quirks.behavior: `select @v = col from t where ...` leaves @v unchanged when no row matches and keeps the LAST row when several match; it never fails.
quirks.target: Keep the previous value when the query returns nothing and take the last row when it returns several; do not throw on an empty or multiple result.
quirks.probe:
declare @v int
select @v = 5
select @v = id from sysobjects where 1 = 2
select 'NXQ|select-assign-from-table|' + convert(varchar(10), @v)

quirks.behavior: A failing statement does not stop the procedure: execution goes on and the program decides with @@error and @@rowcount, which every statement resets.
quirks.target: Read the outcome of each statement right after it (rows affected, error) and continue as the program does; do not let an exception skip the code the legacy runs after the error.

quirks.behavior: Transactions nest by count (@@trancount); a ROLLBACK at any level rolls back everything and sets the count to 0.
quirks.target: Use one transaction for the whole program and roll it back entirely where the program rolls back.
quirks.probe:
begin tran
begin tran
rollback tran
select 'NXQ|nested-tran|' + convert(varchar(10), @@trancount)

quirks.behavior: Comparisons ignore trailing spaces ('a' = 'a  ') and CHAR(n) values are padded with spaces to n.
quirks.target: Compare strings without their trailing spaces and pad or trim CHAR values as the golden master shows.

quirks.behavior: A parameter with a default takes it only when the caller omits the argument; an explicit NULL stays NULL and the default does not apply.
quirks.target: Distinguish an omitted argument (the default applies) from a null one (it stays null): a request field that is absent is not the same as one that is null.
quirks.probe:
exec('create proc nxq_p @a int = 7, @o int output as select @o = @a')
declare @r1 int, @r2 int
exec nxq_p @o = @r1 output
exec nxq_p null, @r2 output
select 'NXQ|param-default-vs-null|' + isnull(convert(varchar(10), @r1), '<null>') + '|' + isnull(convert(varchar(10), @r2), '<null>')
drop proc nxq_p

quirks.behavior: An error raised inside a called procedure (raiserror) does not abort the caller: execution goes on, @@error is 0 after the exec, and only the return status (exec @rc = proc) carries the failure.
quirks.target: Read the status the called program returns and act on it as the legacy does; do not expect an exception from the call, and do not let one abort what the legacy continues.
quirks.probe:
exec('create proc nxq_f as raiserror 20001 ''fallo'' return 5')
declare @rc int, @e int
select @rc = 99
exec @rc = nxq_f
select @e = @@error
select 'NXQ|callee-raiserror-continues|' + isnull(convert(varchar(10), @rc), '<null>') + '|' + convert(varchar(10), @e)
drop proc nxq_f
